egregie.definition: ēgregiē adv. with comp. egregius, excellently, eminently, surpassingly, splendidly, exceedingly, singularly : studere, T.: fecerat hoc: vincere, brilliantly , L.: Dixeris, H.: cordatus, Enn. ap. C.: factus: munitum op…

egregius.definition: ēgregius adj. ex + grex, select, extraordinary, distinguished, surpassing, excellent, eminent : ingenium ad miserias, T.: diligentia: facta, S.: vir: senatus, L.: par consulum, L.: corpus, i. e. in beauty , H.: silent…

egressus2.definition: ēgressus ūs, m egredior, a going out, going away, egress, departure : vestrum egressum ornando: arcet egressu (ventos), O.: egressūs eius explorat, tracks his movements , S.— A disembarking, landing : optimum esse egr…

ehem.definition: ehem interj, ha! what! (in delighted surprise): ehem, tun hic eras? T.

eheu.definition: ēheu interj, ah! alas! (in pain or grief), T.: Eheu sceleris pudet, H.: eheu me miserum, S.

eho.definition: eho interj, look here! look you! holla! soho!: Eho tu, emin ego te? T.: Eho tu inpudens, T.— With enclit. dum., see here now, just look here!: eho dum bone vir, T.

ei1.definition: eī pron. pers., dat. of is.

ei2.definition: ei interj, oh! alas!: Ei, vereor nequid, etc., T.: Ei mihi, quod, etc., O., V., Ct., Tb.

eiaculor.definition: ē-iaculor ātus, ārī, dep., to shoot out, throw out: aquas, O.: se in altum, O.

eicio.definition: ēiciō (pronounced but not written ē-iiciō), iēcī, iectus, ere ex + iacio, to cast out, thrust out, drive away, put out, eject, expel : linguam: eiecto armo, dislocated , V.: ex senatu eiectus: hunc de civitate: a suis…

eiectamentum.definition: ēiectāmentum ī, n eiecto, refuse, jetsam.— Plur. : cetera maris, Ta.

eiectio.definition: ēiectiō ōnis, f eicio, a casting out, banishment, exile .

eiecto.definition: ēiectō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. eicio, to cast out, throw up : harenas, O.: cruorem Ore, V.

eiero.definition: ēierō or ēiūrō āvī , ātus, āre ex + IV-, to refuse upon oath, reject by oath, abjure : id forum sibi iniquum eierare, make oath that the tribunal is prejudiced : me iniquum: bonam copiam, i. e. make oath of insolvency…

eiulatio.definition: ēiulātiō ōnis, f eiulo, a wailing, lamenting : lugubris: non virilis, H.

eiulatus.definition: ēiulātus plur nom., ūs, m eiulo, a wailing, loud lamentation : Philoctetae.

eiulo.definition: ēiulō —, —, āre 2 ei, to wail, lament .

eius.definition: ēius pron. pers., gen. of is.

eiusdem.definition: ēiusdem modī, ēius modī see modus.

elabor.definition: ē-lābor elapsus, ī, dep., to slip away, glide off, fall out, get off, escape: anguis ex columnā elapsus, L.: flexu sinuoso, V.: haec elapsa de manibus nostris: elapsae manibus tabellae, O.: quicquid incidit fastigio m…

elaboratus.definition: ēlabōrātus adj. P. of elaboro, highly wrought, finished, labored : versūs: concinnitas: non elaboratus pes, i. e. a simple strain , H.: alqs in verbis, Ta.

elaboro.definition: ē-labōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to labor, endeavor, struggle, make an effort, take pains: in eā scientiā: in hoc, ut omnes intellegant: ut prosim causis: ut (in me) esse possent, mihi est elaboratum.—To take pains with, work…

elanguesco.definition: ē-languēscō languī, ere, inch, to grow faint, fail, slacken, relax: alienā ignaviā, L.: proelium elanguerat, Cu.: differendo elanguit res, L.

elate.definition: ēlātē adv. with comp. elatus, loftily, proudly : loqui: elatius se gerere, N.

elatio.definition: ēlātiō ōnis, f elatus, a transport, exaltation, elevation : animi: orationis.

elatro.definition: ē-lātrō —, —, āre, to bark out, utter fiercely: quod placet Acriter, H.

elatus.definition: ēlātus adj. P. of effero, exalted, lofty, high : animus: verba, high-sounding : animis superbis, V.: insula opibus, N.

electio.definition: ēlēctiō ōnis, f electus, a choice, selection : verborum: condicionum, of alternatives , L.: legatorum, Ta.

electrum.definition: ēlectrum ī, n , h)/lektron, electrum, an alloy of gold and silver: liquidum, V.: attonitus pro Electro, his plate, Iu.—Amber, a fossil gum from the Baltic sea, O.—Plur: Pinguia, V.

electus1.definition: ēlēctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of eligo, picked, select, choice, excellent : sexaginta (milia armata), picked troops , Cs.: milites, Cs.: exercitūs, Ta.: electissima verba: scripta, Ct.— As subst m. : cum electo …

electus2.definition: (ēlēctus, ūs) m eligo, a choice .—Only abl sing. : necis, O.

elegans.definition: ēlegāns antis, adj. with comp. and sup. for ēligēns, P. of eligo, accustomed to select, fastidious, nice, delicate : heia, ut elegans est! T.: qui se elegantīs dici volunt: elegantissimus poëta, N. — Select, choice, n…

eleganter.definition: ēleganter adv. with comp. and sup. elegans, with good judgment, tastefully, neatly, finely, gracefully, elegantly : lautiores accepti: acta aetas: causam dicere: psallere et saltare elegantius, S.: elegantius facturos…

elegantia.definition: ēlegantia ae, f elegans, taste, propriety, finement, grace, elegance : Attica, T.: ludorum: verborum Latinorum: cum summā elegantiā vivere: conviviorum, Ta.

elegeia.definition: elegēia ae, f , e)legei/a, an elegy, elegiac song: elegeia cantet Amores, O.

elegi.definition: elegī ōrum, m , e)/legoi, elegiac verses, elegy, H., Tb., Pr., O., Ta., Iu.

elementum.definition: elementum ī, n a first principle, simple substance, element: elemento gratulor (i. e. igni), Iu.— Plur., C., O.—Plur, the first principles, rudiments: puerorum: prima, H.: aetatis, i. e. of culture, O.— The beginning,…

elenchus.definition: elenchus ī, m , e)/legxos, a costly trinket, earpendant, Iu.

elephantus.definition: elephantus ī (very rare in nom sing.), and (mostly nom sing.) elephās or elephāns (antis), m , e)le/fas, an elephant: procedebat elephantus in pontem, L.: elephans albus, H.: vires elephanti.—Plur: Indici, T.—Ivory, V.

elevo.definition: ē-levō —, ātus, āre, to lift up, raise: contabulationem, Cs.—Poet.: aura elevat preces, carries away, Pr. — Fig., to lighten, alleviate: aegritudinem.—To make light of, lessen, diminish, impair, trifle with, disparage…

elicio.definition: ēliciō licuī, —, ere ex + lacio, to draw out, entice out, lure forth, bring out, elicit : hostem ex paludibus, Cs.: omnī s citra flumen, Cs.: hostem ad proelium, L.: praemiis ex civitatibus optimum quemque.— To call d…

elido.definition: ēlīdō sī, sus, ere ex + laedo, to strike out, dash out, tear out, force out, squeeze out : auriga e curru eliditur: nubibus ignīs, O.: spuma elisa, dashed up , V.: herbam, O.: nervis morbum, H.— To dash to pieces, sha…

eligo.definition: ēligō lēgī, lēctus, ere ex + 1 lego, to pluck out, root out : stirpes trunco everso eligendae sunt: herbas, Cu.—Fig., to root out : superstitionis stirpes.— To pick out, choose, elect, select, single out : iudices ex …

elimino.definition: ēlīminō —, —, āre ex + līmen, to put out of doors : dicta foras, to blab , H.

elimo.definition: ē-līmō āvī, ātus, āre, to file off, polish, finish: catenas, O. — Fig.: rationes ad tenue elimatae, minutely.

elinguis.definition: ēlinguis e, adj. ex + lingua, tongueless, voiceless, speechless : testis: ex elingui facundum consulem habere, L.: Fannius.

elix.definition: ēlix icis, f ex + 1 LAC-, an artificial watercourse, ditch : prospexit ab elice perdix, O.

elixus.definition: ēlixus adj. ex + LIC-, thoroughly boiled, seethed : assis Miscueris elixa, H.: vervex, Iu.

ellam.definition: ellam for en illam; see en.

elleborus.definition: elleborus (hell-) ī, m, or elleborum, ī, n , e)lle/boros, hellebore (a remedy for mental diseases): Expulit elleboro morbum, H.: triste, Ct. —Plur: graves, V.

ellum.definition: ellum for en illum; see en.

eloco.definition: ē-locō āvī, ātus, āre, to let, farm out: fundum: gens elocata, tributary.

elocutio.definition: ēlocūtiō ōnis, f ex + 4 LAC-, oratorical delivery, elocution .

elogium.definition: elogium ī, n , e)legei=on, an utterance, short saying, maxim: Solonis.—An epitaph: in sepulchro rei p. incisum. — A clause (in a will): de testamento.

eloquens.definition: ēloquēns entis, adj. with sup. P. of eloquor, eloquent : disertos se vidisse multos, eloquentem neminem: homo eloquentissimi: auctores, Ta.

eloquentia.definition: ēloquentia ae, f eloquens, eloquence : summa: quā eloquentiā praeditus.

eloquium.definition: ēloquium ī, n eloquor, expression, utterance, speech : insolitum, H.: tona eloquio, V. — Eloquence : Eloquio virum Molliet, O.: eloquio Nestora vincere, O.

eloquor.definition: ē-loquor ēlocūtus, ī, dep., to speak out, speak plainly, utter, pronounce, declare, state, express: Eloquar an sileam? V.: cogitata praeclare: id quod sentit: unum elocutus, ut tenerent, etc., Cs.: Gratum elocuta cons…

eluceo.definition: ē-lūceō ūxī, —, ēre, to shine out, shine forth, gleam: inter flammas circulus elucens: Elucent aliae (apes), V.—Fig., to shine out, be apparent, be conspicuous, appear, be manifest: scintilla ingeni elucebat in puero:…

eluctor.definition: ē-lūctor ātus, ārī, dep., to struggle out, force a way out: aqua omnis, V.: velut eluctantia verba, i. e. uttered with effort, Ta.—Fig., to surmount, overcome: locorum difficultates, Ta.: tot eluctandae manūs, L.

elucubro.definition: ē-lūcubrō āvī, ātus, āre, to work out at night, toil over: librum, Ta.: causae tamquam elucubratae, well prepared.

elucubror.definition: ēlūcubror ātus, ārī, dep. elucubro, to work out at night, toil over : epistulam.

eludo.definition: ē-lūdō sī, sus, ere, to stop playing, cease to sport: litus, quā fluctus eluderet. — To parry, elude, avoid: quasi rudibus eius eludit oratio (i. e. in a sham fight): elusa volnera, O.—To escape, avoid, shun: celerita…

elugeo.definition: ē-lūgeō ūxī, —, ēre, to have done mourning: quid, cum eluxerunt, sumunt? L.—To mourn for, be in mourning for: patriam.

elumbis.definition: ēlumbis e, adj. ex + lumbus; prop., weak in the loins; of an orator, without energy , Ta.

eluo.definition: ē-luō uī, ūtus, ere, to wash off, cleanse by washing: corpus, O.—To wash away, remove by washing: macula elui non potest: ut sanguis eluatur. —Fig., to wash away, remove, blot out, get rid of: libidinem sanguine: elui…

elutus.definition: (ēlūtus) adj. P. of eluo, washed out, watery . — Only comp: inriguo nihil est elutius horto, H.

eluvies.definition: ēluviēs —, em, ē, f ex + 3 LV-, an overflow, inundation : eluvie mons est deductus in aequor, O.: maris, Ta.: eluvies iter morabantur, Cu.— A washing away, discharge : conducere Siccandam eluviem, removal of sewage , …

eluvio.definition: ēluviō ōnis, f ex + 3 LV-, an overflow, inundation : aquarum: terrarum.

em.definition: em interj., of wonder or emphasis, there!: em tibi, there's for you, T.

emancipo.definition: ē-mancipō or ēmancupō ā vī, ātus, āre, to put out of the paternal authority, declare free, emancipate: filium, L.: filium in adoptionem.— To give up, surrender, abandon: (senectus) si nemini emancipata est: emancipatu…

emano.definition: ē-mānō āvī, ātus, āre, to flow out: fons unde emanat aquaï: ex quo fonte virus emanat, Cu.— Fig., to spring out, arise, proceed, emanate: alio ex fonte praeceptores emanaverunt.—To spread abroad, extend: mala latius. …

ematuresco.definition: ē-mātūrēscō ruī, ere, inch, to ripen, to grow mild, be mitigated: ira Caesaris, O.

emax.definition: emāx ācis, adj. EM-, eager to buy, fond of buying : non esse emacem vectigal est: nemo minus, N.: domina, O.

emblema.definition: emblēma atis (abl plur. matīs), n , e)/mblhma, embossed work, relief, raised ornaments: pocula cum emblemate.— Tessellated work, mosaic: vermiculatum.

embolium.definition: embolium ī, n , e)mbo/lion, an interlude.

emendabilis.definition: ēmendābilis e, adj. emendo, reparable, capable of correction : error, L.

emendate.definition: ēmendātē adv. emendatus, faultlessly, perfectly : loqui.

emendatio.definition: ēmendātiō ōnis, f emendo, a correction, amendment, improvement : philosophiae.

emendator.definition: ēmendātor ōris, m emendo, a corrector, amender : civitatis: noster.

emendatrix.definition: ēmendātrīx īcis, f emendator, she who corrects, a reprover : vitiorum lex.

emendatus.definition: ēmendātus adj. P. of emendo, correct, faultless, perfect : mores: vir, H.: locutio: carmina, H.: emendata maxime.

emendo.definition: ē-mendō āvī, ātus, āre ex + mendum, to free from faults, correct, improve, amend : civitas emendari solet continentiā principum: consuetudinem: res Italas Legibus, H.— To correct, revise : annalīs suos. — To atone for…

ementior.definition: ē-mentior ītus, īrī, dep., to speak falsely, lie, feign, fabricate, falsify, pretend: in historiis: quantum sit ementita opinio, i. e. had erred: auspicia: ementiundo invidiam conflare, S.: vanitas ementiendae stirpis…

emercor.definition: ē-mercor ātus, ārī, dep., to buy up, bribe: hostes, Ta.: avaritiam praefecti, Ta.

emereo.definition: ē-mereō uī, itus, ēre, to obtain by service, earn, merit, deserve: virum, O.: honores, Pr.: emeruit vocis habere fidem, O. — To serve out, complete (a term of service): spes emerendi stipendia, L.: homines emeritis st…

emergo.definition: ē-mergō sī, sus, ere, to bring forth, bring to light, raise up: e gurgite voltūs, Ct.: sum visus emersus e flumine. — Fig., to extricate oneself, raise oneself up, rise: ex malis se, N.: emersus ex tenebris: velut eme…

emeritus.definition: ē-meritus adj., that has finished work, past service: equi, O.: aratrum, O.: acus, Iu.—Plur m. as subst, discharged veterans, Ta.

emetior.definition: ē-mētior mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure out: spatium oculis, V. — To pass, pass over, traverse: tot inhospita saxa, V.: iter, L.: longitudinem Italiae, L.: spatium pedibus, Ta.—P. pass., passed through, traversed: mult…

emeto.definition: ē-metō —, —, ere, to mow away, mow down: plus frumenti agris, H.

emico.definition: ē-micō cuī, cātus, āre, to spring out, spring forth, break forth, leap up: Emicat ex oculis flamma, O.: scaturiges, L.: sanguis in altum, O.: telum nervo, O.: in currum, V.: saxa tormento, L.: carcere, to escape from,…

emigro.definition: ē-migrō āvī, —, āre, to move, depart, emigrate: ex illā domo: domo, Cs.: e vitā .

eminens.definition: ēminēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of emineo, standing out, projecting, prominent, high, lofty : oculi: promunturia, Cs.: saxa, S.: genae leniter: trabes eminentiores, Cs.: per inaequaliter eminentia rupis, irregular s…

eminentia.definition: ēminentia ae, f eminens, a distinctive feature, conspicuous part : nulla.— The lights (in painting).

emineo.definition: ēmineō uī, —, ēre ex + 2 MAN-, to stand out, project, reach upward : eminere et procul videri, Cs.: vetustae radices, S.: hasta in partīs ambas, O.: iugum in mare, Cs.: ex terrā in altitudinem xxx stadia, Cu.: belua p…

eminus.definition: ēminus adv. ex + manus.—Of fighting, aloof, beyond sword reach, at a distance, a spear's-throw off : eminus telis pugnabatur, Cs.: sauciari, S.: certare, Ta.: Dryopem ferit hastā, V.: faces in aggerem iaciebant, Cs.: …

emiror.definition: ē-mīror —, ārī, dep., to gaze at in wonder, stand aghast at: aequora, H.

emissarium.definition: ēmissārium ī, n emitto, an outlet, drain .

emissarius.definition: ēmissārius ī, m emitto, a scout, spy .

emissio.definition: ēmissiō ōnis, f emitto, a projecting, hurling : telorum graviores emissiones habere. — A letting go, releasing : serpentis.

emitto.definition: ē-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to send out, send forth: essedarios ex silvis, Cs.: equitatu emisso, Cs.: pabulatum emittitur nemo, Cs. — To drive, force, hurl, cast, discharge: aculeos in hominem: pila, Cs.: hastam in fin…

emo.definition: emō ēmī, ēmptus, ere EM-, to buy, purchase : domum: mulierem a sectoribus: bene, cheap : male, dear : care, H.: tabernas in publicum, for the public , L.: fundum in diem, on credit , N.: quanti emptast, T.: emit tanti…

emoderor.definition: ē-moderor —, —, ārī, dep., to moderate: dolorem verbis, O.

emodulor.definition: ē-modulor —, —, ārī, dep., to sing, celebrate: Musam, O.

emollio.definition: ē - molliō iī, ītus, īre, to make soft, soften: arcūs, L. — Fig., to soften, make mild, enervate: mores, O.: exercitum, L.: quos nondum pax emollierit, Ta.

emolumentum.definition: ēmolumentum (ēmoli-) ī, n ex + MAL-, gain, profit, advantage, benefit : nullum ad Scamandrum venturum: nullo emolumento impelli in fraudem: ut quam maximum emolumentum novis sociis esset, L.: emolumenta communia.

emoneo.definition: ē-moneō —, —, ēre, to admonish: te ut consequare, etc. (dub.).

emorior.definition: ē-morior —, ī (old, īrī, T.), dep., to die off, die, decease: miserabiliter: emori satius est, T.: maximo cum dolore: per virtutem, S.: ante emoriar, quam, etc., O. — Fig.: quorum laus emori non potest, pass away: amo…

emoveo.definition: ē-moveō mōvī (ēmōstis, L.), mō tus, ēre, to move out, move away, remove, expel, dislodge: multitudinem e foro, L.: cis Volturnum emovendi, L.: magno emota tridenti Fundamenta, stirred, V.—Fig.: pestilentia ex agro Rom…

empiricus.definition: empīricus ī, m , e)mpeiriko/s, a physician guided by experience, empiric.

emporium.definition: emporium ī, n , e)mpo/rion, a place of trade, market-town, market, mart: Puteolanorum.

emptio.definition: ēmptiō ōnis, f EM-, a buying, purchase : falsa: bonorum: mancipiorum, Ta.— A purchase, thing bought : illae emptionis.

emptito.definition: ēmptitō āvī, ātus, āre emo, to buy, purchase : operam, Ta.

emptor.definition: ēmptor ōris, m EM-, a buyer, purchaser : bonorum: emptorem reperire: hians, H.: Dedecorum pretiosus, who pays dearly for , H.

emptum.definition: ēmptum ī, n emptus, a purchase, contract of purchase : quae ex empto aut vendito contra fidem fiunt, in buying and selling .

emulgeo.definition: ē-mulgeō —, ulsus, ēre, to drain out, exhaust: emulso sero, Ct.

emungo.definition: ēmungō nxī, nctus, ere, to wipe the nose, blow the nose: emungeris, Iu.—In the phrase, emunctae naris, clean-nosed, i. e. of nice discernment, of fine taste, H., Ph.—To cheat, swindle: emuncto Simone, H.: argento sene…

emunio.definition: ē-mūniō iī, ītus, īre, to fortify, secure, wall off, strengthen: locus arcis in modum emunitus, L.: obice postes, V.: murus supra ceterae modum altitudinis emunitus, built up, L.—To clear, make passable: silvas ac pal…

en.definition: ēn interj., calling attention, or expressing surprise or indignation, lo! behold! see! there!: en crimen, en causa, cur, etc.: en ego, V., H.: en memoriam sodalis: en causam cur, etc.: en hoc illud est: en cui liberos…

enarrabilis.definition: ēnārrābilis e, adj. enarro, that may be explained, intelligible : textus clipei, V.

enarro.definition: ē-nārrō āvī, ātus, āre, to explain fully, recount, describe, interpret: rem seni, T.: res tuas gestas: alcui somnium.

enascor.definition: ē-nāscor nātus, ī, dep., to grow up, grow out, sprout, spring up, arise: laurea in puppi enata, L.: rami enati, shot out, Cs.: in aede capillus, L.

enato.definition: ē-natō āvī, —, āre, to swim away, escape by swimming: fractis enatat exspes Navibus, H.: pauci enatant, Ph.—Fig.: reliqui enatant tamen, get off.

enavigo.definition: ē-nāvigō āvī, —, āre, to sail away: e scrupulosis cotibus.—To traverse: unda omnibus enaviganda, H.

endo.definition: endo praep. old form of in, in : endo caelo, C. (XII Tabb.).

endoploratus.definition: endoplōrātus P. endoploro, old for imploro, to cry for help : endoplorato, ut, etc., a cry for help having been raised , C. (old form.).

endromis.definition: endromis idis, f , e)ndromi/s, a coarse woollen cloak, athlete's wrapper, Iu.

eneco.definition: ē-necō or ēnicō —, ctus, ā re, to kill off, exhaust, wear out, destroy, torment, plague: enectus siti: squalore enecti, half dead, L.: bos est enectus arando, H.: me rogitando, T.: enicas, you are a plague, T. — Fig.:…

enervatus.definition: ēnervātus adj. P. of enervo, unnerved, weakly, effeminate, unmanly : homines: ratio et oratio: sententia.

enervis.definition: ēnervis e, adj. ex + nervus, nerveless, weak : orator, Ta.

enervo.definition: ēnervō āvī, ātus, āre ex + nervus, to enervate, weaken, make effeminate, deprive of vigor : me enervavit senectus: epulae enervaverunt corpora, L.: undis artūs, O.: vires, H.: ut enervetur oratio compositione verborum.

enim.definition: enim conj. (usu. after the first word in its clause). I. In explaining or specifying, for, for instance, namely, that is to say, I mean, in fact : similis sensus exstitit amoris ... nihil est enim virtute amabilius: n…

enimvero.definition: enim-vērō or enim vērō adv., yes indeed, yes truly, assuredly, of a truth, to be sure, indeed: Enimvero Chremes cruciat adulescentulum, T.: enim vero ferendum hoc quidem non est: hic enim vero tu exclamas, etc.: tum e…

eniteo.definition: ē-niteō tuī, —, ēre, to shine forth, shine out, gleam, brighten: Fruges enitent: egregio decus enitet ore, V.—Fig., to shine forth, be eminent, be displayed, be distinguished: (Athenae) cunctis gentibus enitebant: tan…

enitesco.definition: ēnitēscō -nituī, —, ere, inch. eniteo, to shine forth, become bright, be distinguished : tu enitescis pulchrior multo (Barine), H.: bellum, ubi virtus enitescere posset, display itself , S.: eloquentiae gloriā, Ta.

enitor.definition: ē-nītor -nīxus or -nīsus, ī, dep., to force a way out, struggle upwards, mount, climb, ascend: pede aut manu, L.: in ascensu non facile, Cs.: in altiora, Ta.: impetu capto enituntur, scale the height, L.: Enisus arces…

enixe.definition: ēnīxē adv. with comp. enixus, strenuously, earnestly, zealously : causam suscipere: Caesarem iuvabat, Cs.: enixius ad bellum adiuvare, L.

enixus.definition: ēnīxus adj. P. of enitor, strenuous, earnest, zealous : studium, L.: virtus, L.

eno.definition: ē-nō āvī, —, āre, to swim out, swim away, escape by swimming: e conchā: in terram, L.: Daedalus enavit ad Arctos, flew, V.

enodate.definition: ēnōdātē adv. with comp. enodatus, lucidly, explicitly : narrare: enodatius explicare.

enodatio.definition: ēnōdātiō ōnis, f enodo, an unfolding, development, explanation : nominum.

enodis.definition: ēnōdis e, adj. ex + nodus, free from knots, smooth : trunci, V.: abies, O.

enodo.definition: ēnōdō āvī, ātus, āre enodis, to free from obscurity, explain, elucidate, unfold : nomina: praecepta.

enormis.definition: ēnōrmis e, adj. ex + norma, out of rule, shapeless, irregular : spatium terrarum, Ta.: vici, Ta.— Immense, huge : gladii, Ta.

enotesco.definition: ē - notēscō notuī, —, ere, to become known: quod ubi enotuit, Ta.

ensiger.definition: ēnsiger gera, gerum, adj. ensis + GES-, sword-bearing : Orion, O.

ensis.definition: ēnsis is, m a two-edged sword, brand, glaive: funestus, C. poët.: lateri adcommodat ensem, V.: vanus, L.: strictus, O.

enthymema.definition: enthȳmēma atis, n , e)nthu/mhma, a condensed syllogism, logical argument, Iu.

enubo.definition: ē-nūbō nūpsī, —, ere, to marry away, marry (to a stranger), L.—To marry out of one's rank: filias e patribus, L.

enucleate.definition: ēnucleātē adv. enucleatus, plainly, without ornament : dicere.

enucleatus.definition: ēnucleātus adj. P. of enucleo, pure, clean : suffragia, free from undue influence : genus dicendi, unadorned .

enucleo.definition: ēnucleō —, —, āre ex + nucleus. — Fig., to lay open, explain in detail : haec nunc: argumenta.

enumeratio.definition: e-numerātiō ōnis, f enumero, a counting up, enumerating : argumentorum. — In rhet., a recapitulation .

enumero.definition: ē-numerō āvī, ātus, āre, to reckon up, count over, count out: id, quod ad te rediturum putes, T.: dies, Cs.: quid praeco enumeraret, listed.—To recite, tell at length, recount, relate, detail, describe: istius facta: …

enuntiatio.definition: ēnūntiātiō ōnis, f enuntio.— In logic, a proposition, enunciation .

enuntiatum.definition: ēnūntiātum ī, n P. of enuntio, a proposition .

enuntio.definition: ē-nūntiō āvī, ātus, āre, to speak out, say, express, assert: cum verbo res eadem enuntiatur ornatius: sententias breviter: plane quid sentiam. — To divulge, disclose, reveal, betray: mysteria: iure iurando, ne quis en…

enuptio.definition: ēnūptiō ōnis, f enubo, the right to marry (out of the gens): gentis, L.

enutrio.definition: ē-nūtriō īvī, —, īre, to bring up, nourish, support: puerum, O.

eo1.definition: eō īvī or iī (3d pers. rarely ī t, V.; inf. īvisse or. īsse), itūrus (P. praes. iēns, euntis; ger. eundum), īre 1 I-, to go, walk, ride, sail, fly, move, pass : In in malam rem, T.: subsidio suis ierunt, Cs.: quocumqu…

eo2.definition: eō adv. old dat. and abl. of pron. stem I-. I. Locat. and abl. uses, there, in that place : cum tu eo quinque legiones haberes.—Fig.: res erat eo iam loci, ut, etc., in such a condition.—Therefore, on that account, fo…

eodem.definition: eōdem adv. of place old dat. and locat. of idem. I. Locat. use; with loci, in the same place : res eodem est loci quo reliquisti.— II. Dat. uses, to the same place, to the same point, thither : clientes suos eodem con…

epastus.definition: ē-pāstus adj., eaten up: escae, O.

ephebus.definition: ephēbus ī, m , e)/fhbos, a youth (strictly a Greek from 16 to 20 years of age): greges epheborum: amans, H.: excessit ex ephebis, i. e. reached manhood, T.

ephemeris.definition: ephēmeris idis, f , e)fhmeri/s, a day-book, diary, ephemeris, C., N., O.

ephippiatus.definition: ephippiātus adj. ephippium, riding with a saddle : equites, Cs.

ephippium.definition: ephippium ī, n , e)fi/ppion, a pad-saddle, caparison, rug (as a rider's seat): ephippiis uti, Cs.—Prov.: Optat ephippia bos piger, i. e. envies the horse, H.

ephorus.definition: ephorus ī, m , e)/foros, a Spartan magistrate, one of the five Ephori, C., N.

epicopus.definition: epicōpus adj. , e)pi/kwpos, furnished with oars: phaselus, a row-boat.

epicus.definition: epicus adj. , e)piko/s, epic, heroic: poeta.

epidicticus.definition: epidīcticus adj. , e)pideiktiko/s, for display, declamatory: genus (dicendi).

epigramma.definition: epigramma atis, n (dat. plur. -atis, C.), e)pi/gramma, an inscription: incisum in basi: tripodem ponere epigrammate inscripto, N.—An epigram: in eum facere.

epilogus.definition: epilogus ī, m , e)pilogos, a peroration, epilogue: rhetorum.—Plur: miserabiliores.

epimenia.definition: epimēnia ōrum, n , e)pimh/nia, provisions for a month, rations, Iu.

epiredia.definition: epirēdia ōrum, n e)pi/ + raeda, traces , Iu (acc. to others, carts, wagons ).

epistolium.definition: epistolium ī, n , e)pisto/lion, a short letter, note: Conscriptum, Ct.

epistula.definition: epistula or epistola ae, f , e)pistolh/, a written communication, letter, epistle: Graecis litteris conscripta, Cs.: Verris ad Neronem: epistulam obsignare: mane dare, to send.— Plur., a letter, Ta.

epitaphios.definition: epitaphios ī, m , e)pita/fios, a funeral oration.

epitome.definition: epitomē (once -ma, C.), ēs, f , e)pitomh/, an abridgment, epitome.

epodes.definition: epodes um, m a kind of sea-fish, O.

epops.definition: epops opis, m , e)/poy, a hoopoe, O.

epos.definition: epos (only acc.), n , e)/pos, a heroic poem, H.

epotus.definition: ē-pōtus P., drunk off, drained, exhausted: venenum: medicamentum, L.: epoto poculo: amphora, empty, Ph.: flumina, drunk dry, Iu.: Ter fretum, swallowed up, O.: terreno Lycus hiatu, O.

epulae.definition: epulae ārum, f viands, sumptuous food, dishes, meats: mensae epulis exstruebantur: vino et epulis onerati, S.: exempta fames epulis, V.: vestis, Blattarum epulae, H.: Viscera (voltur) rimatur epulis, ransacks for food…

epularis.definition: epulāris e, adj. epulum, of a feast, at a banquet : accubitio amicorum: sacrificium.

epulo.definition: epulō ōnis, m epulum, a guest at a feast, feaster, carouser , C.— A boon companion : Valerius.—Esp.: Tresviri or Septemviri Epulones, a college of priests to conduct sacrificial banquets , C., L.: Manlius, triumvir ep…

epulor.definition: epulor ātus, ārī, dep. epulum, to feast, banquet, dine : epulantur milites: de die, L.: divisit ad epulandum militibus, L.: dapibus opimis, V.: Ascanium epulandum ponere mensis, as a dish , V.

epulum.definition: epulum ī (only sing.), n a sumptuous meal, banquet, feast, dinner: magnificentissimum: epulum populo dare: Iovis epulum fuit, L.: epulum dare alcui, Iu.

equa.definition: equa ae, f equus, a mare : nobillissimae: Apta quadrigis, H.: Eliades, V.

eques.definition: eques itis, m equus, a horseman, rider : equites, qui litteras attulerant, L.: equus docilis Ire viam quā monstret eques, H.: equitem docuere sub armis Insultare solo, i. e. the horse and his rider , V.— A horse - sol…

equester.definition: equester (-tris, L.) tris, tre, adj. eques, of a horseman, equestrian : statuae. — Of cavalry : proelium, Cs.: tumultus, L.: copiae. — Of the knights of the equestrian order, equestrian, knightly : ordo: locus: ius: f…

equidem.definition: equidem adv. old interj. e + quidem. — In corroboration, verily, truly, indeed, at all events (usu. with 1 st pers. sing .): id equidem ego certo scio, T.: iocabar equidem, T.: equidem negare non possum, etc.: equidem…

equinus.definition: equīnus adj. equus, of a horse, of horses . saeta, a horse-hair : cervix, H.: nervus, a bowstring of horse-hair , V.

equiria.definition: equīria ōrum, n equus, annual races in the Campus Martius, in honor of Mars , O.

equitabilis.definition: equitābilis e, adj. equito, fit for riding, smooth : planities, Cu.

equitatus.definition: equitātus ūs, dat. uī or ū, m equito, cavalry : magnus numerus equitatūs, Cs.: nullus: magnos equitatūs exspectare, large bodies of cavalry , Cs.— The equestrian order, knights : ille: in equitatu recensendo, L.

equito.definition: equitō āvī, ātus, āre eques, to ride, be a horseman, practise riding : in exercitu: uti mos gentis est, S.: Exiguis campis, range , H.: illa (certatio) quā tu contra Alfenum equitabas, manœuvred .—Poet., of the wind, …

equus.definition: equus or ecus ī (gen plur. equōm or equūm, V.), m 3 AC-, a horse, steed, charger : fortis: equis uti: cadere de equo: inanis, without a rider : in equo, mounted : ex equo pugnare, L.— Fig.: conrigam tarditatem cum equ…

era.definition: era (not hera), ae, f erus, the mistress of a house, mistress, lady , T.: errans, Enn. ap. C. — A mistress, ruler : era Fors, Enn. ap. C.: Tritonis, Ct.— A sweetheart , O., Ct.

eradico.definition: ērādīcō —, —, āre ex + radix, to root out, extirpate, annihilate : te, T.

erado.definition: ē-rādō sī, —, ere, to scrape off, shave: genas, Pr.—To erase: Merulam albo senatorio, Ta.—To abolish, eradicate, remove: Curam penitus corde, Ph.: eradenda cupidinis sunt elementa, H.: vitae tempora, consign to oblivi…

erectus.definition: ērēctus adj. with comp. P. of erigo, set up, upright, elevated, lofty : (homines) erectos constituit: voltus, O.: prorae, Cs.—Fig., elevated, lofty, noble : celsus et erectus: ingenium, Ta.: si quis est paulo erectior…

erepo.definition: ē-rēpō rēpsī (pluperf. ē rēpsēmus, H.), —, ere, to crawl over, make a way out of: quos (montīs), H.: totum agrum genibus, Iu.

ereptio.definition: ēreptiō ōnis, f ex + RAP-, a forcible seizure, robbery .

ereptor.definition: ēreptor ōris, m ex + RAP-, a robber, plunderer : bonorum: libertatis.

erga.definition: ergā praep. with acc, towards, in respect of, in relation to: animis te erga, T.: vestra erga me voluntas: erga populum R. fides, Cs.: favor erga nos deorum, Ta.: Quae numquam quicquam erga me commeritast, done me wro…

ergastulum.definition: ergastulum ī, n a workhouse, house of correction, penitentiary: homines ex ergastulis empti: ductus in ergastulum, L.—Plur, the inmates of a workhouse, penitentiary convicts: quibusdam solutis ergastulis, Cs.: inscrip…

ergo.definition: ergō (ergo, O.) subst. and adv. I. As abl. following a gen, in consequence of, on account of, because of, for the sake of (old): lessum funeris ergo habento, C. (lex): dono militari virtutis ergo donari, L. (SC.): ill…

ericius.definition: ēricius ī, m er, a hedgehog, a beam set with spikes, chevaux-de-frise : obiectus portis, Cs.

erifuga.definition: erifuga (heri-) ae, m erus + 2 FVG-, a runaway : famuli, Ct.

erigo.definition: ērigō rēxī, rēctus, ere ex + rego, to raise up, lift, set up, erect, elevate : arborem: hastas, L.: manu mālum de nave, V.: in clivum aciem, lead up , L.: oculos: turrīs, build , Cs.. villas, Iu.: totam aciem, i. e. s…

erilis.definition: erīlis (not herīlis), e, adj. erus, of the head of a family, the master's, mistress's : filius, T.: gressum comitantur erilem, V.: pensum, H.: nomen, O.: sanguis, O.: peccatum, H.

eripio.definition: ēripiō ipuī, eptus, ere ex + rapio, to tear out, snatch away, wrest, pluck, tear, take away : vela, armamenta, copias, Cs.: quae nunc hebetat visūs nubem, V.: ornamenta ex urbibus: sacra ex aedibus: arma ab aliis: ab …

erogatio.definition: ērogātiō ōnis, f erogo, a paying out, distribution : pecuniae.

erogo.definition: ē-rogō āvī, ātus, āre, to appropriate, pay out, pay, expend (usu. from the public treasury): pecunia ex aerario erogata: pecuniam in classem: in eos sumptūs, L.: ei in sumptum.

errabundus.definition: errābundus adj. 1 erro, wandering about, vagrant, at random : errabundi domos pervagarentur, L.: vestigia bovis, V.: agmen, Cu.

erraticus.definition: errāticus adj. 1 erro, wandering, roving, erratic : Delos, O.: lapsu erratico (vitis).

erratio.definition: errātiō ōnis, f 1 erro, a wandering, roving about : hac minor est erratio, T.: nulla in caelo est, nothing moves at random .

errator.definition: errātor ōris, m erro, a wanderer (of the Meander), O.

erratum.definition: errātum ī, n 1 erro, an error, mistake, fault : commune: nullum ob erratum: minimum: errata officiis superes, S.: errata aetatis meae.

erratus.definition: (errātus, ūs) m 1 erro, a wandering, winding .— Only abl plur. : longis erratibus actus, O.

erro1.definition: errō āvī, ātus, āre, to wander, stray, rove, roam: cum vagus et exsul erraret: non certis passibus, O.: circum villulas nostras: per urbem, L.—Pass impers.: solis erratur in agris, V.—Of things: quae (stellae) errante…

erro2.definition: errō ōnis, m 1 erro, a wanderer, vagabond : fugitivus erro, H.— A wanderer in love , Tb.

error.definition: error ōris, m cf. 1 erro, a wandering, straying, strolling : ad quos Ceres in illo errore venisse dicitur: civium: dic Errores tuos, V.: finem rogant erroris, O.: pelagi erroribus actus, V.— A going astray, missing th…

erubesco.definition: ē-rubēscō buī, —, ere, inch, to grow red, redden: saxa erubuisse rosis, O. — To blush with shame, feel ashamed: Erubuit, salva res est, T.: in alquā re: erubuere genae, O.: non est res, quā erubescam, si, etc., L.: ru…

eruca.definition: ērūca ae, f a kind of cole-wort, H., Iu.

eructo.definition: ē-rūctō —, āre, to belch forth, vomit, throw up: saniem, V.: gurges Cocyto eructat harenam, V. — Fig.: sermonibus suis caedem bonorum, make drunken threats of.

erudio.definition: ērudiō īvī, ītus, īre ex + rudis, to educate, instruct, teach, polish : studiosos discendi: alqm in iure: filios ad maiorum instituta: alqm disciplinā, N.: eruditi artibus militiae, L.: me de re p., keep me informed :…

erudite.definition: (ērudītē) adv. eruditus, learnedly, with erudition .—Only comp. and sup: eruditius disputare: litterae eruditissime scriptae.

eruditio.definition: ērudītiō ōnis, f erudio, an instructing, instruction : eius.— Learning erudition : praeclara.

eruditulus.definition: ērudītulus adj. dim. eruditus, somewhat experienced , Ct.

eruditus.definition: ērudītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of erudio, instructed, educated, learned, accomplished , informed, skilled, experienced : quas (artī s) qui tenent eruditi appellantur: Graeculus: rebus gestis: litteris eruditior …

erumpo.definition: ē-rumpō rūpī, ruptus, ere. I. Trans, to cause to break forth, emit, throw out: Canis erumpit ignīs, C. poë .: portis se foras, Cs.: unde se erumpit Enipeus, V.— To break through: nubem, V.: vis piscium Pontum erumpens…

eruo.definition: ē-ruō uī, utus, ere, to cast forth, throw out, root up, dig out, take: humum, O.: sepulcris caprificos, H.: segetem ab radicibus, V.: mortuum: aquam remis, to plough up, O.: illum, to hunt down: quemvis mediā turbā, H…

eruptio.definition: ēruptiō ōnis, f ex + RAP-, a breaking out, bursting forth : ignium: ex oppido, a sally , Cs.: in hostes, L.: ab erupticnibus cavere, Cs.

erus.definition: erus (not herus), ī, m ES-, the master of a house, head of a family ; opp. famuli, C., V., H.— A master, lord, owner, proprietor : propriae telluris, H.: fundus pascat erum, H.: tuus, i. e. husband , Ct.: caelestes, t…

ervum.definition: ervum (her-) ī, n a pulse, bitter vetch, V., H., O.

erythinus.definition: erythīnus ī, m , e)ruthi=nos, a red sea-mullet, O.

esca.definition: ēsca ae, f ED-, a dish (prepared for the table), food, victuals, viands, meat, bait : temperatae escae: contemptissimae: dulcis, V.: prima, course , H.—Fig.: Plato escam malorum appellat voluptatem.

escaria.definition: ēscāria ōrum, n esca, dishes, plate , Iu.

escendo.definition: ēscendō (exs-) endī, ēnsus, ere ex + scando, to climb up, mount, ascend : in caelum: in rostra: quo cum escendisset, L.: equos, S.: Oetam, L.: rostra, Ta.: Ilium a mari, to go up , L.: Delphos, L.

escensio.definition: ēscēnsiō ōnis, f ex + SCAND-, an ascension, mounting, climbing, going up : escensionem a Paesto facere, L.: ab navibus in terram, a landing , L.: quibus (classibus) escensiones in agros factae erant, incursions , L.

escensus.definition: (ēscēnsus, ūs) m ex + SCAND-, a scaling . — Only abl sing. : capta escensu munimenta, by storm , Ta.

esculentus.definition: ēsculentus adj. esca, fit for eating, good to eat, edible : frustra.—Plur n . as subst, food .

escunt.definition: escunt old for erunt; see sum.

essedarius.definition: essedārius ī, m essedum, a fighter in a war-chariot , C., Cs.

essedum.definition: essedum ī, n, and (poet.) esseda, ōrum Celtic, a two-wheeled war-chariot, car (of Gauls and Britons), Cs., L., V.; sometimes displayed at Rome, C., H., O.

esurio.definition: ēsuriō —, ītūrus, īre, desid. 1 edo, to desire to eat, suffer hunger, be hungry, hunger : esurientibus ceteris: num esuriens fastidis omnia? H.: est spes nos esurituros satis, T.: Nil quod nobis esuriatur, O.: divitia…

esuritio.definition: ēsurītiō ōnis, f esurio, a hungering, hunger , Ct.

et.definition: et adv. and conj. I. adv., adding to a fact or thought, also, too, besides, moreover, likewise, as well, even: Ph. vale. Pa. et tu bene vale, T.: ‘tu tuom negotium gessisti bene.’ Gere et tu tuom bene: et Caelius prof…

etenim.definition: et-enim conj., adding an independent and emphatic clause, as a reason, explanation, or corroboration, for, for truly, and indeed, because, since: etenim iste non audebat, etc.: etenim quid est, quod amplius exspectes?…

etesiae.definition: etēsiae ārum, m , e)thsi/ai, Etesian winds, trade-winds, N. W. winds which prevail in summer in the eastern parts of the Mediterranean Sea: venti: etesiis tenebatur, Cs.

ethologus.definition: ēthologus adj. , h)tholo/gos, imitating manners, mocking personal peculiarities: mimi.

etiam.definition: etiam adv. (rarely conj.) et + iam. I. Of time, now too, yet, as yet, even yet, still, even now : incertus sum etiam quid sim facturus, T.: cum iste etiam cubaret, introductus est: Invalidus etiamque tremens, etiam in…

etiamdum.definition: (etiamdum, etiamnum, etiamnunc, etiamsī, etiamtum) see etiam IV.

etsi.definition: et-sī conj. I. Introducing a concession, though, although, albeit: Etsi scio ego meum ius esse ... ego tamen, etc., T.: etsi non iniquum est, tamen est inusitatum: etsi aliquo accepto detrimento, tamen, etc., Cs.: ets…

eu.definition: eu interj., eu)=, bravo! well! well done!: Eu noster, laudo, T.: ‘eu!’ that's right, H.

eugae.definition: eugae (euge) interj., eu)=ge, bravo! well done! good! hurrah!: eugae habeo optumam, T. — Ironic.: eugae, iam lepidus vocor, excellent! T.

euhans.definition: euhāns or euāns antis P. (the cry of the Bacchantes), crying euhan! Ct., Pr.—Poet. with acc: euhantīs orgia Ducebat Phrygias, celebrating the rites of Bacchus with the cry euhan! V.

euhoe.definition: euhoe or euoe (disyl.; not ēvoe), interj., eu)oi=, the cry of revellers at the festivals of Bacchus, V., H., O., Ct.

eunuchus.definition: eunūchus ī, m , eu)nou=xos, a eunuch, T., Cs., C., Iu.—Fem., a comedy of Terence.

euripus.definition: eurīpus (-os) ī, m , eu)/ripos, a channel, strait, narrow sea.

eurous.definition: eurōus adj. eurus, eastern, orient : fluctus, V.

eurus.definition: eurus ī, m , eu)=ros, the southeast wind, H.— Plur., V., O.—The east wind: Eurus ad Auroram recessit, O. — Wind: Rhipaeus, V.

evado.definition: ē-vādō sī (evāstī, H.), sus, ere, to go out, come out, go forth: ex balineis: oppido, S.: undis, V.: in terram, disembark, L. — With acc, to traverse, pass, leave behind: viam, V.: vada, O.: castra, L.: silvas, Ta.: a…

evagor.definition: ē-vagor ātus, ārī, dep., to wander forth, march to and fro, manœuvre: effuse, L.: ad evagandum spatium, for evolutions, L. — Fig., to spread, extend: qui appetitū s longius evagantur: late vis morbi, L. — With acc: or…

evalesco.definition: ē-valēscō luī, —, ere, inch, to grow strong: ut quaeque gens evaluerat, Ta. — Fig., to grow, develop, ripen: multa secutura quae adusque bellum evalescerent, Ta.: nationis nomen evaluisse, came into vogue, Ta.: tempus…

evalidus.definition: ē-validus adj., very strong, mighty: spina.

evanesco.definition: ē-vānēscō nuī, —, ere, inch, to vanish, pass away, die away, disappear: (vinum) vetustate, to become uapid: Cornua lunae, O.: in tenuem ex oculis evanuit auram, V.— Fig., to pass away, be forgotten, perish, be wasted:…

evanidus.definition: ēvānidus adj. VAC-, vanishing, passing away : pectora, O.: amor, O.

evasto.definition: ē-vāstō āvī, ātus, āre, to lay utterly waste, devastate: urbīs, L.: culta evastata sunt bello, L.

eveho.definition: ē-vehō vexī, vectus, ere, to carry out, bring forth, convey out, lead forth: omnia (signa) ex fanis evecta: ex planis locis aquas, L.: incaute se evehentīs excipiebat, rushing out, L.—To carry up: in collem evehi, L.—…

evello.definition: ē-vellō vellī, volsus or vulsus, ere, to tear out, pluck out, extract: linguam Catoni: ferrum, Cs.: arbor, quā evolsā, L.: spinas agro, H.: Pollicibus fauces, O.: emblema, to tear away. — Prov.: Caeno plantam, H. — Fi…

evenio.definition: ē-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come out, come forth: Merses profundo, pulchrior evenit, H.— Fig., to fall out, come to pass, happen, befall, betide: si tibi evenerit quod metuis ne accidat: ut alia Romae eveniat saepe …

eventum.definition: ēventum ī, n P. n. of evenio, an occurrence, chance, event : causae eventorum.— That which befalls, experience, fortune : te ex nostris eventis communibus admonendum: pendere ex alterius eventis.— An issue, consequenc…

eventura.definition: ēventūra ōrum, n P. n. of evenio, that which will happen : eventura precor, i. e. my prayers shall be fulfilled , Tb.

eventus.definition: ēventus ūs, m ex + BA-, an occurrence, accident, event, fortune, fate, lot : fore eos eventūs rerum qui acciderunt: ex eventu navium, Cs.: ducis, V.: qui quosque eventū s exciperent, Cs.: impiorum fratrum, L.: eventūs…

everbero.definition: ē-verberō —, —, āre, to strike violently, beat: clipeum alis, V.: cineres alis, O.: hastis os, Cu.

evergo.definition: ē-vergō —, —, ere, to send out, cause to meander forth: ut montes evergerent rivos, L.

everriculum.definition: ēverriculum ī, n ex + VAR-, a broom, sweep . — Only fig.: malitiarum omnium, dragnet : huiusce modi (a play on the name of Verres).

everro.definition: ē-verrō verrī, versus, ere, to sweep out.— Fig., to clean out, strip, plunder: fanum eversum relinquere: paratus ad everrendam provinciam.

eversio.definition: ēversiō ōnis, f ex + VERT-, an overthrowing, subversion : columnae: rerum p.

eversor.definition: ēversor ōris, m ex + VERT-, a subverter, destroyer : regnorum, V.: rei p.

eversus.definition: ēversus. 1. P. of everro.— 2. P. of everto.

everto.definition: ē-vertō or ēvortō tī, sus, ere, to overturn, upturn, turn upside down: navem: aequora ventis, V.: aquas, O.: eversas cervicīs tuas abstine, refrain from twisting your neck, T.—To overturn, overthrow, upset, throw down…

evestigatus.definition: ē-vestīgātus P., traced out, discovered, O.

evidens.definition: ē-vidēns adj. with comp. and sup, looking out, obvious, apparent, manifest, plain, clear, evident: si quid est evidens, de quo inter omnīs conveniat: res, L.: numen, L.: quid est evidentius?: evidentissimum id fuit, q…

evidenter.definition: ēvidenter adv. evidens, evidently, manifestly, obviously : paenitere, L.

evidentia.definition: ēvidentia ae, f evidens.—In rhet., distinctness, vivid presentation .

evigilo.definition: ē-vigilō āvī, ātus, āre, to be wakeful, be vigilant: in studio.—To watch over, watch through: tua consilia quam evigilata cogitationibus, with what vigilance matured: nox evigilanda, Tb.: quos (libros) studium evigila…

evilesco.definition: ē-vīlēscō luī, —, ere, inch, to become vile, grow worthless: cuius criminationibus eviliussent pericula sua, had been depreciated, Ta.

evincio.definition: ē-vinciō nxī, nctus, īre, to bind up, wind around: diademate caput, Ta. — Usu. P. pass.: evincti bracchia duces, fettered: viridi olivā, garlanded, V.: Puniceo suras cothurno, V.: vittā crinīs, O.: palmae, bound with …

evinco.definition: ē-vincō vīci, vīctus, ere, to overcome, conquer, subdue, vanquish, overwhelm: evicit omnia miles, L.: lacrimis evicta meis, V.: blandimentis vitae evicta (i. e. ad vivendum), Ta.: evinci ambitu in gaudium, to be force…

eviro.definition: ē-virō āvī, —, āre ex + vir, to emasculate : corpus, Ct.

eviscero.definition: ē-vīscerō —, ātus, āre ex + viscera, to deprive of entrails, disembowel, eviscerate : corpus, Enn. ap. C.: columbam pedibus uncis, mangle , V.

evitabilis.definition: ēvītābilis e, adj. 1 evito, avoidable : telum, O.

evito1.definition: ē-vītō āvī, ātus, āre, to shun, avoid: meta Evitata rotis, H.: fraxinum, O.: causas suspicionum: tela amictu, Ct.

evito2.definition: ēvītō āvī, —, āre ex + vita, to deprive of life, kill : Priamo vi vitam evitari, Enn. ap. C.

evocator.definition: ēvocātor ōris, m evoco, a summoner, recruiter, one who drums up civium perditorum.

evocatus.definition: ēvocātus adj. P. of evoco, called out.— Plur. m . as subst, reënlisted veterans , Cs., S.

evoco.definition: ē-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call out, call forth, summon, evoke: te huc foras, T.: milites ex hibernis in expeditionem, S.: virum e curiā, L.: testīs huc: nostros ad pugnam, challenge, Cs.: deus evocatus sacratis sibi f…

evolgo.definition: ē-volgō (-vulgō) āvī, ātus, āre, to make commonly known, divulge: civile ius, L.: sic evulgari iussit, laurum additum (esse), etc., Ta.: evolgatus pudor, i. e. public exposure, Ta.

evolo.definition: ē-volō āvī, ātus, āre, to fly out, fly away, fly up: ex quercu (aquila): sic evolat ales, O.— To come forth quickly, rush forth, hasten out: ex omnibus partibus silvae, Cs.: e conspectu: e poenā, to escape: rus ex urb…

evolsio.definition: ēvolsiō (ēvul-) ōnis, f ex + 2 VEL-, a pulling out : dentis.

evolutio.definition: ēvolūtiō ōnis, f ex + 3 VOL-, an unrolling : poētarum, reading .

evolvo.definition: ē-volvō volvī, volūtus, ere, to roll out, roll. forth, unroll, unfold: amnis ... in mare evolvendo terram, etc., L.: vestī s tyranni, O.: volumen epistūlarum: aquas per campos, to spread, Cu.: In mare se (Xanthus), di…

evomo.definition: ē-vomō uī, itus, ere, to spew out, vomit forth: eas (conchas): partem maris ore, O. — To spew out, eject, expel, disgorge: quod (urbs) tantam pestem evomuerit: Faucibus fumum, V.—Fig., to vent, disgorge: iram in eos, …

ex.definition: ex or (only before consonants) ē praep. with abl, out of, from within (opp. in). I. In space, out of, from: signa ex urbe tollere: solem e mundo tollere: ex hoc fonticulo tantumdem sumere, H.: ex Aethiopiā Ancillula, …

exacerbo.definition: ex-acerbō āvī, ātus, āre, to exasperate, irritate, provoke: ut irā exacerbarentur animi, L.: contumeliis hostes, L.

exactio.definition: exāctiō ōnis, f ex + 1 AG-, a driving out, expelling : (regum).— A driving, conduct, supervision : operum publicorum.—Fig., a collecting, exaction : pecuniae: earum (pecuniarum), L.: frumenti, Ta. — A tax, tribute, im…

exactor.definition: exāctor ōris, m ex + 1 AG-, a driver-out, expeller : regum, L.—Fig., a demander, exactor : supplici, an executioner , L.: promissorum, L.: cum ipse ut exactor circumiret, overseer , L.— A collector of taxes, tax-gathe…

exactus.definition: exāctus adj. with comp. P. of exigo, precise, accurate, exact : numerus, L.: fides, O.: morum exactior, O.—Plur n . as subst: sociis exacta referre, V.

exacuo.definition: ex-acuō uī, ūtus, ere, to sharpen, make pointed: vallos, V.: spicula, V. — Fig., to sharpen, make keen, stimulate, excite, inflame: mucronem in nos: ingeni aciem ad bona diligenda: plurimos irā, N.: animos in bella, H…

exadversus.definition: ex-adversus (-vorsus) adv. and praep, over against, opposite.—As adv.: pistrilla, et exadvorsum fabrica, T.: exadvorsum ei loco Tonstrina erat, T.—As praep. with acc: exadversus eum locum: exadversum Athenas, N.

exaedificatio.definition: exaedificātiō ōnis, f exaedifico, a finishing, completing (of a building).—Fig.: posita in rebus et verbis.

exaedifico.definition: ex-aedificō āvī, ātus, āre, to finish building, complete, erect, build, construct: oppidum, Cs.: domos, S.: templa deum, L.: mundum. — Fig., to finish, complete: opus.

exaequatio.definition: exaequātiō ōnis, f exaequo, a likening, uniformity (of dress, etc.), L.

exaequo.definition: ex-aequō āvī, ātus, āre, to make equal, place on a level, equal: se cum inferioribus: tironi sese exaequari sinere, L.: militibus exaequatus cum imperatore labos, S.: iura pretio, i. e. to sell alike. —To equal, attai…

exaeresimus.definition: exaeresimus adj. , e)caire/simos, that may be taken out, to be omitted: dies, intercalary.

exaestuo.definition: ex-aestuō āvī, ātus, āre, to boil up, foam up, ferment: exaestuat mare, L.: unda ima verticibus, V.: mens irā, V.: ignis (amoris), O.

exaggeratio.definition: exaggerātiō ōnis, f exaggero.—Only fig., elevation, exaltation : animi.

exaggero.definition: ex-aggerō āvī, ātus, āre, to heap, pile, load, fill: planitiem aggestā humo, Cu.: spatium, Cu. —To heap up, accumulate: fortunas: opes, Ph. — Fig., to exalt, amplify, heighten, magnify, exaggerate: sextulam suam nimiu…

exagitator.definition: exagitātor ōris, m exagito, a severe critic, censurer : rhetorum.

exagito.definition: ex-agitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq, to rouse, keep in motion, disquiet, harass, persecute, disturb, torment, vex: istius iniuriis exagitati: ab Suevis exagitati, Cs.: rem p. seditionibus, S.: di exagitent me, Si, etc., H.:…

exalbesco.definition: ex-albēscō buī, ere, inch, to turn pale: metu, Enn. ap. C.: in principiis dicendi.

examen1.definition: exāmen inis, n ex + 1 AG-, a multitude flying out, swarm : apium: vesparum, L.: cum prima sui ducent examina reges, V.— A multitude, crowd, shoal, swarm : examinibus suis agros operire, L.: iuvenum, H.: servorum.

examen2.definition: exāmen inis, n ex + 2 AG-, the tongue of a balance : aequato examine lances Sustinet, V.—Fig., a weighing, consideration : legum, O.

examino.definition: exāminō āvī, ātus, āre 2 examen, to weigh : (aër) tamquam paribus examinatus ponderibus: ad certum pondus, Cs.—Fig., to weigh, ponder, consider, examine, try, test : omnia verborum momentis, non rerum ponderibus: verb…

exanclo.definition: exanclō (not-antlō), āvī, ātus, āre, to exhaust, suffer through, endure: tot belli annos, C. poët: multa, quae corpore exanclata atque animo pertuli!: omnīs labores.

exanimatio.definition: exanimātiō ōnis, f exanimo, faintness, terror : metum subsequens: in exanimationes incidere.

exanimis.definition: exanimis e, adj. ex + anima, lifeless, dead : (columba) Decidit exanimis, V.: ut exanimem labentem ex equo Scipionem vidit, L.: artūs, O.— Fig., breathless, terrified, dismayed : legiones vice unius, with suspense for…

exanimo.definition: exanimō āvī, ātus, āre exanimus, to put out of breath, tire fatigue, weaken, exhaust . — Only pass: ut cursu milites exanimarentur, Cs.— To breathe forth : exiliter verba.— To deprive of life, kill, wear out : taxo se…

exanimus.definition: exanimus adj. ex + anima, lifeless, dead : iuvenis, V.: strata corpora, corpses , L.

exardesco.definition: ex-ārdēscō ārsī, ārsus, ere, inch, to blaze out, kindle, take fire: materies facilis ad exardescendum.— Fig., to be kindled, be inflamed, break out, be exasperated, be provoked, rage: iracundiā ac stomacho: dolore, Cs…

exaresco.definition: ex-ārēscō ruī, —, ere, inch, to dry up, become dry: amnes: fontes, Cs.—Fig., to dry up, wither, perish: exustus flos siti veteris ubertatis exaruit: vetustate exaruit (opinio).

exarmo.definition: ex-armō —, —, āre, to disarm: cohortes, Ta.

exaro.definition: ex-arō āvī, ātus, āre, to plough out, dig up, dig out: sepulcra: puerum. — To raise, produce, obtain by tillage, harvest: tantum labore suo frumenti: decem medimna ex iugero. — Fig., to mark on tablets with the style,…

exaspero.definition: ex-asperō āvī, ātus, āre, to make rough, roughen: exasperato fluctibus mari, L.: fretum, O.—Fig., to irritate, provoke, exasperate: durati tot malis exasperatique, L.: animos, L.

exauctoro.definition: ex-auctōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to discharge from service, release from the military oath: exercitus velut exauctoratus morte ducis, L.: milites exauctorati, L.: se, i. e. to quit the service, L.: exauctorati tribuni, cash…

exaudio.definition: ex-audiō īvī, ītus, īre, to hear clearly, distinguish, discern, hear: voces: sonitum remorum, Cs.: voces mulierum, L.: maximā voce, ut omnes exaudire possint, audible to all.— To hear, perceive, understand, attend to,…

exaugeo.definition: ex-augeō —, —, ēre, to increase greatly, confirm: opinionem mihi animo, T.

exauguratio.definition: exaugurātiō ōnis, f exauguro, a desecrating, profaning : sacellorum, L.

exauguro.definition: ex-augurō —, —, āre, to desecrate, make profane: fana sacellaque, L.

excaeco.definition: ex-caecō āvī, ātus, āre, to blind, make blind: nos.—To put out of sight: Flumina excaecata, lost underground, O.

excandescentia.definition: excandēscentia ae, f excandesco, kindling wrath, an outbreak of anger , Cs.

excandesco.definition: ex-candēscō duī, —, ere, inch, to grow hot, kindle.—Fig.: nisi irā excanduit fortitudo.

excanto.definition: ex-cantō —, ātus, āre, to charm forth, enchant: sidera excantata, H.: puellas, Pr.

excarnifico.definition: ex-carnificō —, ātus, āre, to tear to pieces, butcher: me, i. e. torment, T.: Anaxarchum.

excavo.definition: ex-cavō —, ātus, āre, to hollow out: ex unā gemmā trulla excavata.

excedo.definition: ex-cēdō cessī (excēssis for excesseris, T.), cessus, ere, to go out, go forth, depart, retire, withdraw: abiit, excessit: metu, L.: quoquam ex istoc loco, T.: ex tenebris in lucem: ex itinere, Cs.: acie, Cs.: bello, S…

excellens.definition: excellēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of excello, towering, prominent, distinguished, superior, surpassing, excellent : animus ac virtus: vir virtute: inter tot unus: studium, Cs.: cycnus, of surpassing beauty …

excellenter.definition: excellenter adv. with comp. excellens, excellently, exceptionally well : quae gesta sunt: pronuntiare, N.: se excellentius gerere.

excellentia.definition: excellentia ae, f excellens, superiority, excellence : animi.—Plur: (in amicitiā).

excello.definition: excellō (praes. excellet, Cu.), —, celsus, ere 2 CEL-, to be eminent, be superior, surpass, excel : qui (artifex) excellit: haec (flagitia) quae excellunt, your most conspicuous crimes : super ceteros, L.: ceteris: in…

excelse.definition: (excelsē) adv. excelsus, in an elevated tone, loftily .— Only comp: excelsius dicere.

excelsitas.definition: excelsitās ātis, f excelsus, loftiness, ascendency : animi.

excelsus.definition: excelsus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of excello, elevated, lofty, high : locus, T.: mons, Cs.: vertex montis, V.: signum: in excelsiore loco: cornu excelsius, Cs.: mons excelsissimus, Cs.—As subst n., a height : simul…

exceptio.definition: exceptiō ōnis, f ex + CAP-, an exception, restriction, limitation : sine ullā exceptione: imperitare nullis exceptionibus, i. e. with absolute power , Ta.: in lege.—Esp., in law, a limitation (in a declaration or comp…

excepto.definition: exceptō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. excipio, to take out, take up, catch : barbatulos de piscinā: hos (milites), Cs.: auras, to snuff up , V.

excerno.definition: ex-cernō —, crētus, ere, to sift out, separate, part: ex captorum numero excreti Saguntini, L.: excreti a matribus haedi, V.

excerpo.definition: excerpō psī, ptus, ere ex + carpo, to pick out, extract : semina pomis, H.—Fig., to pick out, choose, select, gather : ex ipsis (malis), si quid inesset boni: nomina ex tabulis, L.— To take out, leave out, except, omi…

excessus.definition: excessus ūs, m 1 CAD-, a departure, demise : e vitā : Romuli.— A digression , Ta.

excetra.definition: excetra ae, f a snake, serpent, dragon, C. poë t.—In reproach, of a woman, L.

excidium.definition: excidium (exsci-) ī, n 2 SAC-, overthrow, demolition, subversion, ruin, destruction : urbis, L.: Troiae, V.: gentis, Ta.: arces excidio dare, V.: petit urbem excidiis, V.

excido1.definition: excidō cidī, —, ere ex + cado, to fall out, drop down, fall away : sol excidisse mihi e mundo videtur: dentīs Excidere videre, H.: mihi Excidit cera, from my hand , O.: Palinurus Exciderat puppi, V.: in flumen (sc. e …

excido2.definition: excīdō īdī, īsus, ere ex + caedo, to cut out, cut off, hew out, cut down : arbores, Cs.: excisa arbor: columnas rupibus, V.— To raze, demolish, lay waste, destroy : aedīs: Troiam, V.: Sugambros, Ta.—Fig., to drive out…

excieo.definition: ex-cieō and ex-ciō īvī, ītus and itus, ī re, rarely ēre (imperf. excībat, L.), to call out, summon forth, rouse: consulem ab urbe, L.: animas sepulcris, V.: artifices e Graeciā, Cu.: Antiochum in Graeciam, L.: Volscos…

excipio.definition: excipiō cēpī, ceptus, ere ex + capio. I. To take out, withdraw : alqm e mari: clipeum sorti, V. —Fig., to rescue, release, exempt : servitute exceptus, L.: nihil libidini exceptum, Ta. — To except, make an exception, …

excisio.definition: excīsiō ōnis, f ex + 2 SAC-, a destroying : tectorum: urbium.

excitatus.definition: excitātus adj. with comp. P. of excito, lively, vehement, excited : sonus: clamor excitatior, L.: fortuna, rising .

excito.definition: excitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. excio, to call out, summon forth, bring out, wake, rouse : me e somno: sopitum mero regem, Cu.: scuto offenso excitatus vigil, L.: reum consularem, summon : testīs ab inferis: cervum latib…

excitus.definition: excitus and excītus P. of excieo and excio.

exclamatio.definition: exclāmātiō ōnis, f exclamo. — In rhet., an exclamation , C., Ta.

exclamo.definition: ex-clāmō āvī, ātus, āre, to call out, cry aloud, exclaim: contiones saepe exclamare vidi, applaud loudly: illa exclamat, ‘minume gentium,’ T.: Latine exclamat nostros frustra pugnare, S.: exclamavisse, ut bono essent …

excludo.definition: exclūdō sī (exclūstī for exclū sistī, T.), sus, ere ex + claudo, to shut out, exclude, cut off, remove, separate : aliquem e portu: ab re frumentariā Romanos, Cs.: Capua impios civīs exclusit: laurea Excludet ictūs (s…

exclusio.definition: exclūsiō ōnis, f ex + CLAV-, a shutting out, exclusion , T.

excogitatio.definition: excōgitātiō ōnis, f excogito, a thinking out, contriving, inventing : excogitationem non habent difficilem, may be thought out without difficulty .

excogito.definition: ex-cōgitō āvī, ātus, āre, to think out, contrive, devise, invent: nihil contra rem p.: quid mali aut sceleris excogitari potest, etc.: ad haec: multa ad avaritiam excogitabantur, Cs.: in rebus excogitandis, N.: excogi…

excolo.definition: ex-colō coluī, cultus, ere, to cultivate, improve, ennoble, refine, perfect: omni vitā atque victu excultus: excultus doctrinā: lanes rudes, O.: regio ad luxum exculta, Cu.: vitam per artes, V.: orationem, Ta. — To wo…

excoquo.definition: ex-coquō coxī, coctus, ere, to boil out, melt out, dry up: Tam excoctam (ancillam) reddam, dried up, T.: ignis vitium metallis excoquit, O.: omne per ignīs vitium, V.: ferrum, quod excoquit ignis, tempers, O.

excors.definition: excors cordis, adj. ex + cor, without intelligence, without understanding, senseless, silly, stupid : anus: hoc qui non videt, excors est: admodum: turpis et excors, H.

excrementum.definition: excrēmentum ī, n ex + 2 CER-, an excretion : oris aut narium, Ta.

excresco.definition: ex-crēscō —, —, ere, to grow up: in hos artūs, Ta.: haedi, V.

excrucio.definition: ex-cruciō āvī, ātus, āre, to torment, torture, rack, plague: servos fame, Cs.: vinculis excruciatum necare: ipsos crudeliter, Cs.—Fig., to distress, afflict, harass, trouble, vex, torment: meae me miseriae excruciant:…

excubiae.definition: excubiae ārum, f ex + CVB-, a lying out on guard, watching, keeping watch : cuius excubias et custodias mei capitis cognovi: vigilum canum Tristes, H.— A watch, watchmen : vigilum excubiis obsidere portas, V.: divōm a…

excubitor.definition: excubitor ōris, m ex + CVB-, a watchman, guard, sentinel : (castella) excubitoribus tenebantur, Cs.

excubo.definition: ex-cubō buī, bitum, āre, to lie out of doors, camp out: in agro. — To lie out on guard, keep watch, watch: pro castris, Cs.: ad mare, Cs.: per muros, V.: excubitum in portas cohortīs mittere, S.: (Cupido Chiae) Pulchr…

excudo.definition: ex-cūdō dī, sus, ere, to strike out, hammer out: silici scintillam, V. — To hatch out: pullos ex ovis. — To forge, mould: spirantia aera, V.: gladios, Iu.— To prepare, make: ceras, V.—Fig., to compose: alqd: librum, Ta.

exculco.definition: exculcō —, —, āre ex + calco, to tread down, stamp firm , Cs.

excurro.definition: ex-currō cucurrī or currī, cursus, ere, o run out, run forth, hasten forwards: excurrat aliquis, qui hoc nuntiet: ad me: in Pompeianum, make an excursion: excurso spatio, traversed, T.—Esp. in war, to sally forth, mak…

excursio.definition: excursiō ōnis, f 1 CEL-, a running out, running forth . (oratoris) moderata eaque rara, i. e. a stepping forwards. — A sally, excursion, inroad, invasion, expedition : equitatū s: ex oppido, Cs.: finīs ab excursionibu…

excursor.definition: excursor ōris, m 1 CEL-, a skirmisher, scout, spy : istius.

excursus2.definition: excursus ūs, m 1 CEL-, a running out, running forth, excursion : excursūsque brevīs temptant (apes), V.— A sally, charge, inroad, invasion : militum, Cs.: subiti, Ta.

excusabilis.definition: excūsābilis e, adj. excuso, that may be excused, excusable : delicti pars, O.

excusate.definition: (excūsātē) adv. excuso, without blame .— Only comp: excusatius excipere, Ta.

excusatio.definition: excūsātiō ōnis, f excuso, an excusing, excuse : turpis: iusta: Aeduis dat veniam excusationemque accipit, Cs.: iniuriae: Pompei, Cs.: excusatio Sulpici legationis obeundae, a declining : aetatis: valetudinis: excusati…

excuso.definition: excūsō āvī, ātus, āre ex +*causo; 1 CAV- —With pers. obj., to excuse, make an excuse for : Atticae me: se de consilio, Cs.: me apud Apuleium: ut excuser morbi causā: si iudex excusetur Areopagites esse, pleads as his …

excussus.definition: excussus adj. P. of excutio, stretched out, stiff : lacertus, O.

excutio.definition: excutiō cussī, cussus, ere ex + quatio, to shake out, shake off, cast out, drive out, send forth : (litteris) in terram excussis, shaken out : equus excussit equitem, threw off , L.: Excutimur cursu, V.: lectis utrumq…

exedo.definition: ex-edō ēdī, ēsus, ere, to eat up, consume, devour: tibi omne est exedendum, i. e. take the consequences, T.— To prey upon, consume, destroy: alquem adsidue, consume the property of, T.: id vis aliqua exedet: urbem, V.…

exedra.definition: exedra ae, f , e)ce/dra, a hall furnished with seats, parlor.

exedrium.definition: exedrium (exhe-) ī, n , e)ce/drion, a sittingroom, parlor: exedria nova in porticulā.
