expromo.definition: ex-prōmō prōmpsī, prōmptus, ere, to show forth, discover, exert, practise, exhibit, display: supplicia in civīs: apparatūs supplicii, L.: vigilandi laborem in cenis.—To give utterance to, utter, disclose, express, sta…

expromptus.definition: exprōmptus adj. P. of expromo, ready, at hand : malitia atque astutia, T.

expugnabilis.definition: expūgnābilis e, adj. expugno, that may be taken by assault, assailable : urbs, L.: arx magnis exercitibus, Ta.

expugnatio.definition: expūgnātiō ōnis, f expugno, a taking by assault, storming : urbis, Cs.: hostilis. — Plur: aedificiorum.

expugnator.definition: expūgnātor ōris, m expugno, a stormer, capturer : urbis.—Fig.: pudicitiae.

expugnax.definition: (expūgnāx, ācis) adj. expugno, victorious, effectual .—Only comp: expugnacior herba, O.

expugno.definition: ex-pūgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to take by assault, storm, capture, reduce, subdue: urbīs per vim, Cs.: Cirtam armis, S.: quam (turrim), V.: iuvenum domos, H.: ipsum caput, i. e. the old man in person, H.—To subdue, overcome…

expulsio.definition: expulsiō ōnis, f 1 PAL-, a driving out, expulsion : Laenatis.—Plur: civium.

expulsor.definition: expulsor ōris, m 1 PAL-, a driver out, expeller : bonorum: tyranni, N.

expultrix.definition: expultrīx īcis, f expulsor, she that expels : philosophia vitiorum.

expurgo.definition: ex-pūrgō āvī, ātus, āre, to purge, cleanse, purify: me, i. e. cure of poetic ecstasy, H. — Fig.: expurgandus est sermo.—To clear from censure, exculpate, vindicate, justify, excuse: me, T.: sese parum, fail to vindica…

exquiro.definition: exquīrō sīvī, sītus, ere ex+quaero, to search out, seek diligently, inquire into, scrutinize, inquire, ask : ex te causas divinationis: haec nimis a Graecis, to be too exacting in : Ancillas cruciatu, T.: secum, quid …

exquisite.definition: exquīsītē adv. with comp. exquisitus, carefully, accurately, particularly, excellently : de eo crimine disputare: quae (rationes) exquisitius conliguntur.

exquisitus.definition: exquīsītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of exquiro, carefully sought out, ripely considered, choice, excellent, exquisite : sententia: iudicium litterarum: munditia nimis: exquisitius dicendi genus: laudari exquisitiss…

exsacrifico.definition: ex-sacrificō (-cruficō) —, —, āre, to sacrifice: hostiis balantibus, Enn. ap. C.

exsaevio.definition: ex-saeviō —, —, īre, to cease raging: dum reliquum tempestatis exsaeviret, L.

exsanguis.definition: ex-sanguis (exang-) e (no gen. or dat; in plur. only nom.), adj., without blood, bloodless, lifeless: corpora mortuorum: umbrae, V.—Pale, wan, exhausted, feeble: genae: exsanguis et mortuus concidisti: metu, O.: visu,…

exsarcio.definition: ex-sarciō or exerciō —, rtūrus, īre, to patch, mend, repair: sumptum suom, repay their cost, T.

exsatio.definition: ex-satiō āvī, ātus, āre, to satisfy, glut, sate: exsatiati cibo, L.: clade exsatiata domus, O.: patruum sanguine domūs, Ta.

exsaturabilis.definition: exsaturābilis e, adj. exsaturo, that may be sated : nec exsaturabile pectus, insatiate , V.

exsaturo.definition: ex-saturō (exat-) —, ātus, āre, to satisfy satiate, sate: belua exsaturanda visceribus meis, O.: exsaturata lubido, Poët. ap. C.: eius supplicio animum: odiis exsaturata quievi, V.

exscindo.definition: ex-scindō or excindō idī, issus, ere, to extirpate, annihilate, destroy: templum sanctitatis: quae urbs se exscindi pateretur: finī s tuos, L.: ferro gentem, V.: virtutem, Ta.

exscribo.definition: ex-scrībō (excr-) īpsī, īptus, ere, to write out, write off, copy: tabulas: exscribendi potestas.

exsculpo.definition: ex-sculpō or exculpō psī, ptus, ere, to dig out, cut out, chisel out, carve: nescio quid e quercu. —To scratch out, erase: versūs, N.—Fig., to elicit, extort: ex aliquo verum, T.

exseco.definition: ex-secō or execō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut out, cut away, remove: vitiosas partīs: linguam: cornu exsecto frons, H.: nervis urbis exsectis: Lichan iam matre peremptā, V.—To cut, castrate: alqm. —To deduct, take out, exto…

exsecrabilis.definition: exsecrābilis (execr-) e, adj. exsecror, accursed : fortuna, L.— Cursing, execrating : carmen, L.: odium in bis captos, i. e. bitter , L.

exsecratio.definition: exsecrātiō (execr-) ōnis, f exsecror, an execration, malediction, curse : Thyestea.— An oath with imprecation : hunc exsecratione devinxerat: post execrationem degustare, S.

exsecratus.definition: exsecrātus (execr-) adj. P. of exsecror, accursed, execrable, detestable : populo R.: columna.

exsecror.definition: exsecror or execror ātus, ārī, dep. ex + sacro, to curse, utter curses, execrate, abhor : te: Catilinae consilia, S.: terram Ulixi, V.: in se, L.: haec in se: ut pereat Atreus: verba exsecrantia, O.— To take an oath w…

exsectio.definition: exsectiō (exect-) ōnis, f 2 SAC-, a cutting out, excision : linguae: fundi.

exsecutio.definition: exsecūtiō ōnis, f exsequor, an accomplishing : negotii, Ta.: Syriae, i. e. absolute power in , Ta.

exsequiae.definition: exsequiae or exequiae ārum, f SEC-, a funeral procession, funeral obsequies : convenire ad exsequias cohonestandas: Ante urbem exsequiae Significant luctum, O.: fertur in exsequiis matrona, O.: exsequiis rite solutis,…

exsequialis.definition: exsequiālis (exequ-) e, adj. exsequiae, of a funeral, funereal : carmina, dirges , O.

exsequor.definition: ex-sequor or exequor cūtus, ī, dep., to follow to the grave: Hunc omni laude, C. poët.— Fig., to follow, follow after, accompany, go after, pursue: cladem illam fugamque: fatum illius, i. e. share: suam quisque spem, …

exsero.definition: ex-serō ruī, rtus, ere, to stretch out, thrust out, put forth, take out: manum ad mentum, L.: bracchia aquis, O.: via quā se exsereret, come forth, O. —Fig.: se aere alieno.—P. perf., thrust out, protruding, bare, unc…

exserto.definition: exsertō —, —, āre, freq. exsero, to stretch out, thrust forth : Ora, V.

exsibilo.definition: ex-sībilō —, —, āre, to hiss out, hiss from the stage: histrio exsibilatur.

exsiccatus.definition: exsiccātus adj. P. of exsicco, dried up, dry, jejune : orationis genus.

exsicco.definition: ex-siccō āvī, ātus, āre, to dry up, make dry: arbores.—To drink up: vina culullis, H.

exsigno.definition: ex-sīgnō —, ātus, āre, to write out, note down: sacra omnia exsignata, L.

exsilio.definition: exsiliō or exiliō iluī, —, īre ex + salio, to spring out, spring forth, leap up, start up, bound : ad te, T.: de sellā: domo levis exsilit, H.: protinus, O.: (anguis) in siccum, V.: gaudio: exsiluere oculi, started ou…

exsilium.definition: exsilium or exilium ī, n exsul, banishment, exile : exsili poena: confugere in exsilium: civium, L.: civīs in exsilium eicio: in exilio aetatem agere, S.: esse in exsilio: quendam de exsilio reducere: revocare, L.: Ex…

exsisto.definition: ex-sistō or existō stitī, —, ere, to step out, come forth, emerge, appear: e latebris, L.: ab inferis: (bovis) a mediā fronte cornu exsistit, Cs.: nympha gurgite medio, O.: occultum malum exsistit, comes to light. — T…

exsolvo.definition: ex-solvō or exolvō solvī, solūtus, ere, to loose, unloose, set loose, release, deliver, free: te, T.: venas, to open, Ta.: toto paulatim se corpore, V. —Fig., to solve, resolve: nodum erroris, L.: obsidum, raise, Ta.:…

exsomnis.definition: exsomnis (exom-) e, adj. ex+somnus, sleepless, watchful : Vestibulum servat, V.: Euhias, H.

exsorbeo.definition: ex-sorbeō or exorbeō uī, —, ēre, to suck out, suck up, drain, drink: Pectora linguis, O.: civilem sanguinem.— Fig., to seize greedily: praedas. — To exhaust: viros, Iu. — To meet eagerly, welcome: difficultatem.

exsors.definition: ex-sors or exors sortis, adj., without lot, not assigned by lot: te voluit exsortem ducere honores (i. e. praeter ordinem), V. (al. honorem).— Having no share in, free from, deprived of: dulcis vitae, V.: amicitiae, L…

exspatior.definition: ex-spatior (expat-) ātus, ārī, dep., to wander from the way, spread, extend: exspatiantur equi, O.: Exspatiata flumina, i. e. overflowing, O.

exspectatio.definition: exspectātiō or expectātiō ōnis, f exspecto, an awaiting, expecting, expectation, longing, desire : caeca: praeter exspectationem, unexpectedly : magna: cum summā exspectatione populi R.: exspectationibus decipiendis: …

exspectatus.definition: exspectātus adj. with sup. P. of exspecto, anxiously expected, longed for, desired, welcome : carus omnibus exspectatusque venies: seges, V.: exspectati ad amplissimam dignitatem fratres, i. e. thought worthy of the h…

exspecto.definition: ex-spectō or expectō āvī, ātus, āre, to look out for, await, wait for : diem ex die, ut statuerem: alius alium exspectantes, S.: eventum pugnae, Cs.: ultima semper Exspectandi dies homini est, O.: cenantes comites, i.…

exspersus.definition: exspersus P. ex-sparsus, sprinkled, splashed : sanieque exspersa natarent Limina, V.

exspes.definition: ex-spēs adj. (only nom sing.), without hope, hopeless: inops, exspes, O.: enatat exspes, H.

exspiratio.definition: exspīrātiō (expīr-) ō nis, f exspiro, a breathing out, exhalation : terrae.

exspiro.definition: ex-spīrō or expīrō āvī , ātus, āre, to breathe out, emit, blow out, exhale, give out: medios animam in ignīs, O.: flammas pectore, V.: Vis ventorum Exspirare aliquā cupiens, escape, O.—To breathe one's last, expire: e…

exsplendesco.definition: ex-splendēscō duī, ere, inch, to shine forth, be distinguished: clarius, N.

exspolio.definition: ex-spoliō āvī, ātus, āre, to spoil, pillage, plunder: urbem: hos vestro auxilio, Cs.: virtutem rerum selectione.

exspuo.definition: ex-spuō uī, ūtus, ere, to spit out, spit: vina, Iu.: hamum, O.—Fig., to expel, banish: miseriam ex animo, T.

exsterno.definition: exsternō āvī, ātus, āre 2 STAR-, to terrify greatly, affright : alqm luctibus, Ct.: (Io) se exsternata refugit, O.

exstillo.definition: ex-stīllō or extīllō ā vī, ātus, āre, to trickle away, melt: lacrumis si extillaveris, T.

exstimulator.definition: exstimulātor (ext-) ōris, m exstimulo, an inciter, instigator : rebellionis, Ta.: Verginii, Ta.

exstimulo.definition: ex-stimulō (ext-) āvī, ātus, āre, to goad on, instigate, stimulate: virum dictis, O.: Tigris Exstimulata fame, O.: fata cessantia, i. e. hasten death, O.

exstinctio.definition: exstinctiō ōnis, f STIG-, extinction, annihilation .

exstinctor.definition: exstinctor ōris, m STIG-, an extinguisher : incendi. — An annihilator, suppressor : patriae: latrocini.

exstinctus.definition: exstinctus (ext-) adj. P. of exstinguo, dead : Exstinctus amabitur, H.: Amphion, O.— Plur m . as subst: violare exstinctos, O.

exstinguo.definition: ex-stinguō or extinguō nxī (exstinxstī for exstinxistī, exstinxem for exstinxissem, V.), nctus, ere, to put out, quench, extinguish: lumina: ignis exstinguitur, goes out: ignem, V.— To deprive of life, kill, destroy: …

exstirpo.definition: ex-stirpō (ext-) āvī, ātus, āre, to root out, eradicate, extirpate: arbores, Cu. — Fig.: vitia: ex animo humanitatem.

exsto.definition: ex-stō or extō —, —, āre, to stand out, stand forth, project, protrude, extend above, tower: (milites) cum capite solo ex aquā exstarent, Cs.: super aequora celso collo, O.: summo pectore, Cs.: ferrum de pectore, O. —…

exstructio.definition: exstrūctiō or extrūctiō ō nis, f exstruo, a building up, erecting, structure : ea, quae, etc.— Plur: tectorum.

exstructum.definition: exstrūctum ī, n exstructus, a lofty seat : exstructoque resedit, V.

exstruo.definition: ex-struō or extruō ūxī, ūctus, ere, to pile, heap up, accumulate: materiam pro vallo, Cs.: acervum (librorum): exstructos disiecit montīs, V.: exstructis in altum divitiis, H.: tapetibus altis Exstructus, on a pile of…

exsuctus.definition: exsūctus P. ex-sugo, drawn out, extracted, dried : medulla, H.: Ossa exsucta medullis, Iu.

exsudo.definition: ex-sūdō or exūdō āvī, ā tus, āre, to ooze, exude: exsudat inutilis umor, V. — To perform with sweating, toil through, undergo: causas, H.: certamen, L.

exsul.definition: exsul or exul ulis, m and f 2 SAL-, a banished person, wanderer, exile : capitis damnati exsulesque, Cs.: exsules restituti: pauper et exsul, homeless , H.: patriae quis exsul Se quoque fugit? H.: mundi, O.: nunc vero…

exsulo.definition: exsulō or exulō āvī, ātum, āre exsul, to be an exile, be banished, live in exile : Romae: in Volscos exsulatum abiit, L.: apud Prusiam: Protei ad usque columnas, V. — To be absent, be a stranger : domo, T.: animo.

exsultans.definition: exsultāns (exult-) ntis, adj. P. of exsulto, boastful, vainglorious : animus, Ta.: supra modum, Ta.

exsultatio.definition: exsultātiō (exult-) ōnis, f exsulto, a leaping for joy, exultation , L.: Athamantis: par, Ta.

exsultim.definition: exsultim adv. 2 SAL-, leaping about, friskingly : ludit exsultim, H.

exsulto.definition: exsultō or exultō āvī, —, āre, freq. exsilio, to spring vigorously, leap up, jump up : equi ferocitate exsultantes: taurus in herbā, O.: in limine Pyrrhus, V.: exsultant aestu latices, V.: exsultantes undae, dancing ,…

exsuperabilis.definition: exsuperābilis (exup-) e, adj. exsupero, to be overcome : non exsuperabile saxum, V.

exsuperantia.definition: exsuperantia (exup-) ae, f exsupero, preeminence, superiority : virtutis.

exsupero.definition: ex-superō or exuperō āvī, ātus, āre, to mount up, tower: exsuperant flammae, V. — To surmount, pass over: iugum, V.: solum Helori, V. —Fig., to be superior, prevail, be conspicuous, excel: si non poterunt exsuperare, …

exsurdo.definition: exsurdō —, —, āre ex+surdus, to deafen, dull, blunt : palatum, H.

exsurgo.definition: ex-surgō or exurgō surrēxī, —, ere, to rise up, rise, get up, stand up: cum exsurgeret, simul, etc.: exsurge quaeso: ex insidiis, L.: temere, Ta.: altior, V.—Of the sun, Ta.: presso tellus aratro, Tb.: cum geminis exs…

exsuscito.definition: ex-suscitō (exusc-) āvī, ātus, āre, to rouse from sleep, awaken: te gallorum cantus exsuscitat.— To kindle: flammas aurā, O.: incendium, L. —Fig., to stir up, rouse up, excite: animos: animum dictis.

exta.definition: exta ōrum, n sup. for *ecista from ex, the chief internal organs of the body, significant organs (in prognostication): exta interpretari: dare, L.: inspicere: reddere Marti, V.: lustralia, V.: victimae, L.

extabesco.definition: ex-tābēscō buī, ere, inch, to pass away completely, disappear: corpus macie extabuit, Poët. ap. C.—Fig.: opiniones diuturnitate.

extemplo.definition: extemplō adv. ex+*tempulum, dim. of tempus, immediately, straightway, forthwith, without delay : quid fingat extemplo non habet: haec extemplo in invidiam, verterunt, L.: Dixit et extemplo sensit, etc., at once , V.: …

extemporalis.definition: extemporālis e, adj. ex+tempus, off hand, on the spur of the moment : audacia, Ta.

extendo.definition: ex-tendō tendī, tentus or tēnsus, ere, to stretch out, spread out, extend: extensis digitis: Buten harenā, stretch prostrate, V.: capita tignorum, Cs.: Maiores pennas nido, H.: aciem latius, Cu.: labellum, pout, Iu.: …

extentus.definition: extentus adj. with sup. P. of extendo, extended, extensive, wide : latius Lucrino Stagna lacu, H.: extentissima vallis, L.

extenuatio.definition: extenuātiō ōnis, f extenuo, a lessening, diminution, extenuation (as a figure of speech).

extenuatus.definition: extenuātus adj. with sup. P. of extenuo, trifling, faint, weak : vestigia, Ct.: oratio, Her.: (copiolae) extenuatissimae, Brut. ad C.

extenuo.definition: ex-tenuō āvī, ātus, āre, to make small, reduce, diminish: aër extenuatus, rarefied: in aquas, O.: mediam aciem, L.: extenuatā acie, S. — Fig., to diminish, lessen, weaken, extenuate, detract from: laudes verbis: cuius…

exter.definition: (exter or exterus, tera, terum) adj. ex, on the outside, outward, of another country, foreign, strange . — Only plur: ius nationum exterarum: civitates: regna, V.; see also exterior, extimus, extremus.

exterebro.definition: (ex-terebrō) —, ātus, āre, to extract by boring, bore out: aurum.

extergeo.definition: (ex-tergeō) —, sus, ēre, to strip clean, plunder: fanum extersum relinquere.

exterior.definition: exterior us, adj. comp. exter, outward, outer, exterior : vallus, Cs.: contra exteriorem hostem, Cs.: comes exterior, i. e. on the left side , H.

exterius.definition: exterius adv. exterior, on the outer side, without : sitae (urbes), O.

extermino.definition: exterminō āvī, ātus, āre ex+terminus, to drive out, drive away, expel, exile, banish : Marcellum ex urbe: oppugnatores rei p. de civitate.—Fig., to drive out, put away, put aside, remove : auctoritatem vestram e civit…

externus.definition: externus adj. exter, outward, external : visio<*> vir rebus externis laudandus, foreign relations .—As subst m. : odium in externos, towards strangers .— As subst n. : externi ne quid, H.: illa externa, outward goods.…

extero.definition: ex-terō —, —, ere, to tread down, crush: nives, O.

exterreo.definition: ex-terreō uī, itus, ēre, to strike with terror, frighten, affright: praeter modum exterreri: urbem nuntius exterruit, Ta.: voltu legiones, Ta.: propriā exterrita voce est, i. e. lost her voice through fright, O.: Impr…

extimesco.definition: ex-timēscō muī, —, ere, inch, to be greatly afraid, fear greatly, await with fear, dread: equi repentinis sibilis extimescebant: de fortunis: ne id evenerit: Non extimui, quod, etc., V.: si filius venisset, posse exti…

extimus.definition: extimus or extumus adj. sup. ex, outermost, farthest, most remote : orbis. — Plur n . as subst: umor Extuma possedit, O.

extispex.definition: extispex icis, m exta + SPEC-, an observer of entrails, diviner, soothsayer .

extollo.definition: ex-tollō —, —, ere, to lift out, lift up, raise, elevate: iacentem: caput: pugionem, Ta.: in gremium liberorum ex te genus, Enn. ap. C.: gurgite palmas, Pr.—Fig., to raise, exalt: novos, S.: opibus et honoribus extoll…

extorqueo.definition: ex-torqueō sī, tus, ēre, to twist out, wrench out, wrest away: ferrum e manibus: horum gladios: dextrae mucronem, V.: in servilem modum extorti, wrenched, L.: extorque, put me to the torture, T.—To obtain by force, ex…

extorris.definition: extorris e, adj. ex + terra, driven out of the country, exiled, banished, homeless : hinc extorres profugerunt: agro Romano, L.: patriā domo, S.: extorre hinc Punicum nomen, driven from this land , L.: extorrem populu…

extortor.definition: extortor ōris, m TARC-, an extorter : Bonorum, T.

extortus.definition: extortus adj. P. of extorqueo, deformed , puella, Iu.

extra.definition: extrā adv. and praep. exter. I. Adv. (for comp. see exterius), on the outside, without : extra et intus hostem habere, Cs.: et in corpore et extra: illa, quae sunt extra, outward goods .—In the phrase, extra quam: ext…

extraho.definition: ex-trahō āxī, āctus, ere, to draw out, draw forth, pull out, drag: telum e corpore: telum de volnere, O.: puerum alvo, H.: consulem ex tectis: rure in urbem, H.: senatores vi in publicum, L.: extractos ad certamen fud…

extraneus.definition: extrāneus adj. exter, from without, strange : nullum extraneum malum est: ornamenta.—As subst m., a stranger , L.— Plur., Ta.

extraordinarius.definition: extra-ōrdinārius adj., out of the common order, extraordinary, uncommon: pecuniae: reus, to be tried out of the usual order: cohortes, select, L.: porta (i. e. praetoria), L.: petitio consulatūs: imperium: periculum, Cu.

extrarius.definition: extrārius adj. extra, outward, external, extrinsic : res (opp. in corpore). — As subst m., a stranger , T.

extremitas.definition: extrēmitās ātis, f extremus, the extremity, end, terminus : mundi.—In geometry, the surface .

extremo.definition: extrēmō adv. extremus, at last, finally Hamilcarem imperatorem fecerunt, N.

extremum.definition: extrēmum adv. extremus, at last, finally , C.: liquefacta Tabuit, O.— For the last time : te adfari, V.: Adloquor amicos, O.

extremus.definition: extrēmus adj. sup. exter, outermost, utmost, extreme, farthest, last : oppidum Allobrogum, Cs.: finis provinciae, L.: Indi, H.: in codicis extremā cerā: extremā lineā amare, i. e. to make love at a distance , T.: vini…

extrico.definition: ex-trīcō āvī, ātus, āre ex + tricae, to disentangle, extricate, clear, free : extricata densis Cerva plagis, H.: nummos unde unde, procure with difficulty , H.—Fig., to unravel, clear up : nihil, Ph.

extrinsecus.definition: extrīnsecus adv. exter + secus, from without, from abroad : obiectā terribili re: spiritum adducere: imminens bellum, L.— Without, on the outside : inaurata (columna).

extrudo.definition: ex-trūdō sī, sus, ere, to thrust out, push forth, drive out, drive away: me foras, T.: Pollucem, get rid of: extrudi a senatu in Macedoniam: extruso mari aggere, shut out, Cs.: merces, to sell off, H.

extumefactus.definition: extumefactus adj. ex-tumeo + facio, swollen : (pars animi) potu (B. & K.).

extundo.definition: ex-tundō tudī, —, ere, to beat out, strike out, forge out: nobis hanc artem, devise, V.: ancilia, fashion in relief, V.: calcibus frontem, crush, Ph.: fastidia, drive off, H.

exturbo.definition: ex-turbō āvī, ātus, āre, to drive out, thrust out, drive away, thrust away: homines e possessionibus: alqm focis patriis: provinciā exturbatus: caede animas, O.: spem pacis, L.—To drive away (a wife), divorce: Octavia…

exubero.definition: ex-ūberō —, —, āre uber, to grow luxuriantly, be abundant, abound, overflow : luxuriā foliorum exuberat umbra, V.: alte spumis amnis, V.: pomis annus, V.: ex eruditione eloquentia, Ta.: animus fenore, revels , Ta.

exulcero.definition: ex-ulcerō āvī, ātus, āre, to make worse, exasperate, embitter: quae sanare nequeunt: exulceratus animus.

exululo.definition: ex-ululō —, ātus, āre, to howl, cry out, howl violently, O.—P. pass.: (Bacchis) exululata iugis, after howling, O.: mater, invoked with screams, O.

exundans.definition: exundāns ntis, adj. P. of exundo, overflowing, abundant : ingenii fons, Iu.

exundo.definition: ex-undō āvī, —, āre, to flow out, overflow: tura in litora exundant, are washed up, Ta.—Fig.: exundat eloquentia, Ta.

exuo.definition: exuō uī, ūtus, ere 4 AV-, to draw out, take off, pull off, put off : pharetram umero, O.: iugum, shake off , L.: caestū s, V.— To unclothe, divest, free, put forth : pellibus membra, H.: ossa lacertosque, bares , V.: …

exuro.definition: ex-ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere, to burn out, burn up, consume: vivus exustus est: vicos: classem, V. —To dry up: loca exusta solis ardoribus, S.: paludem, V.—To consume, destroy: aliis scelus exuritur igni, V.: cornua, O.: e…

exustio.definition: exūstiō ōnis, f exustus, a burning up, conflagration : exustiones terrarum.

exuviae.definition: exuviae ārum, f 4 AV-, that which is stripped off, clothing, equipments, arms : pyram Erige exuviasque omnīs super imponant, V.: (coluber) positis novus exuviis, his slough , V.: leonis, skin , V.: ferarum, O.: devota…

exuvium.definition: exuvium ī, n 4 AV-, spoils, booty : exuvio plenus ab hoste redis, Pr.
